bib.title: Video-ChatGPT: Towards Detailed Video Understanding via Large Vision and Language Models

question: Can an LLM be adapted to hold detailed conversations about videos, and how can such models be evaluated quantitatively?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning a pooled-CLIP-feature adapter on a high-quality video-instruction set gives better temporal and spatial video conversation than concurrent models.
contributions: Video-ChatGPT, a video conversation model with spatiotemporal pooled CLIP features
100,000 video-instruction pairs via human-assisted and semi-automatic annotation
First quantitative video conversation evaluation framework

method.summary: LLaVA (CLIP ViT-L/14 + Vicuna-v1.1 7B) is fine-tuned on 100K video-instruction pairs, updating only a linear projection. Frame features are average-pooled over space (T tokens) and time (N tokens) and concatenated to T+N visual tokens.

datasets.name: Video-instruction data (ActivityNet-200 subset enriched)
datasets.source: ActivityNet-200 captions; released under MIT licence (promised)
datasets.preprocessing: Human: annotators enrich captions. Semi-auto: Katna keyframes, BLIP-2 and GRiT frame captions, Tag2Text tag filtering (Swin-B, 384x384, threshold 0.7), GPT-3.5 merges captions and generates QA with in-context examples.

datasets.name: ActivityNet-200 test set with dense captions and QA
datasets.source: Curated from ActivityNet-200 with human QA

datasets.name: MSVD-QA, MSRVTT-QA, TGIF-QA FrameQA, ActivityNet-QA
datasets.source: Xu et al. 2017; Jang et al. 2017; Yu et al. 2019

other.visual_tokens: T+N, N=h*w, patch size 14; T, resolution not stated
other.trainable: linear layer only; encoder and LLM frozen

training.objective: autoregressive next-token loss on answer tokens

metrics.name: GPT-judged score on 5 aspects
metrics.definition: GPT-3.5 scores output 1-5 for correctness, detail orientation, contextual understanding, temporal understanding, consistency

metrics.name: Zero-shot QA accuracy and score
metrics.definition: GPT-assisted evaluation of open-ended answers: accuracy plus relative score 1-5

eval.protocol: Single run, no seeds or significance tests; GPT-3.5 judge, replicated with Vicuna-1.5 13B; blind human test on 50 videos.

availability.data: promised to release under MIT licence

results.claim: Annotators could distinguish human from semi-automatic QA pairs only at near chance.

limits: Struggles with subtle temporal relationships in long videos (> 2 min)
Difficulty recognising details of small objects
Judge prompts, T, resolution, optimizer and schedule not given; single run, no seeds
Judge swap changes absolute scores (consistency 2.37 vs 3.09) and the open-source judge omits LLaMA Adapter
